title: Energy, Work and Power
seo_title: Secondary 3 Physics: Energy, Work and Power Worksheets (O-Level 6091 with Answers)
standard_text: Show understanding that energy can be stored in different stores and transferred by mechanical work, electrical work, heating and radiation; state and apply the principle of conservation of energy; recall and apply kinetic energy = ½mv² and gravitational potential energy = mgh; recall and apply work done = force × distance moved in the direction of the force and power = work done ÷ time taken; calculate efficiency; describe renewable and non-renewable energy resources and their advantages and disadvantages (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Physics 6091 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 O-Level Physics worksheets on energy: energy stores, conservation of energy, kinetic and potential energy, work done, power, efficiency and energy resources. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Energy is never created or destroyed.
key_sub: KE = ½mv², GPE = mgh, W = Fd, P = E ÷ t.
body_html:
How to think about it

Energy is transferred between stores but the total stays the same.

  • Kinetic energy = ½mv². Gravitational potential energy = mgh (g = 10 N/kg).
  • Work done = force × distance moved in the direction of the force (J). Power = work done ÷ time (W = J/s).
  • Efficiency = useful energy output ÷ total energy input × 100%. Wasted energy is usually thermal energy.
  • Renewable resources (solar, wind, hydro) are replaced naturally; fossil fuels and nuclear fuel will run out. Singapore uses mainly natural gas.
Example

A 2 kg ball moves at 6 m/s. KE?

½ × 2 × 6²

Answer: 36 J

Example

A 5 kg box is lifted 3 m. Gain in GPE?

5 × 10 × 3

Answer: 150 J

Example

A ball falls 5 m. Speed at the bottom?

mgh = ½mv²

v = √(2 × 10 × 5)

Answer: 10 m/s

Common mistakes

  • Writing KE = mv² and forgetting the ½.
  • Saying work is done when an object does not move.
  • Mixing up power and energy: power is energy per second.
  • Giving an efficiency above 100% after dividing the wrong way round.

faq.a: Divide the useful energy (or power) output by the total energy (or power) input and multiply by 100%.

faq.q: How do kinetic and potential energy change when an object falls?
faq.a: Gravitational potential energy is transferred to kinetic energy. Without air resistance, mgh lost = ½mv² gained.

faq.q: Is solar energy useful in Singapore?
faq.a: Yes. Singapore is sunny all year, so solar panels on rooftops and floating on reservoirs are its main renewable resource, but most electricity still comes from natural gas.

items.q: Which energy changes happen in a battery-powered torch?
c: chemical potential energy → electrical → light and thermal energy
chemical potential energy → thermal → kinetic → electrical energy
gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy
kinetic energy → thermal energy (heating the brakes)
items.e: A battery-powered torch: chemical potential energy → electrical → light and thermal energy.

items.q: Is tidal energy a renewable or a non-renewable energy resource?
c: neither: it is not an energy resource
items.e: A renewable resource is replaced naturally and will not run out; fossil fuels and nuclear fuel will run out.

items.q: Which energy changes happen in a stretched catapult firing a stone?
c: gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy
chemical potential energy → gravitational potential energy (and thermal)
items.e: A stretched catapult firing a stone: elastic potential energy → kinetic energy.

items.q: What is work done?
c: force × distance moved in the direction of the force

items.q: Is work done when you hold a heavy bag still?
c: No: the bag does not move in the direction of the force.
Only if the bag is very heavy.
items.e: No distance moved, no work done (on the bag).

items.q: Is oil a renewable or a non-renewable energy resource?
c: neither: it is not an energy resource
items.e: A renewable resource is replaced naturally and will not run out; fossil fuels and nuclear fuel will run out.

items.q: Why can no machine be more than 100% efficient?
c: It is not allowed by law.
Energy cannot be created, so useful output cannot exceed input.

items.q: Which energy changes happen in a ball falling from a height?
c: chemical potential energy → thermal → kinetic → electrical energy
chemical potential energy → electrical → light and thermal energy
kinetic energy → thermal energy (heating the brakes)
items.e: A ball falling from a height: gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy.

items.q: Which energy changes happen in a person climbing stairs?
c: chemical potential energy → electrical → light and thermal energy
chemical potential energy → gravitational potential energy (and thermal)
items.e: A person climbing stairs: chemical potential energy → gravitational potential energy (and thermal).

items.q: Which energy changes happen in a gas-fired power station?
c: chemical potential energy → thermal → kinetic → electrical energy
items.e: A gas-fired power station: chemical potential energy → thermal → kinetic → electrical energy.

items.q: Is hydroelectric energy a renewable or a non-renewable energy resource?
c: neither: it is not an energy resource
items.e: A renewable resource is replaced naturally and will not run out; fossil fuels and nuclear fuel will run out.

items.q: Which energy store increases when a lift raises passengers?
Which energy store does a moving car have?
Is biomass a renewable or a non-renewable energy resource?
c: neither: it is not an energy resource
items.e: A renewable resource is replaced naturally and will not run out; fossil fuels and nuclear fuel will run out.

items.q: State the principle of conservation of energy.
c: Energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only be transferred from one store to another.
Energy is always created in power stations.
Energy is used up when work is done.
items.e: The total energy stays the same.

items.q: Which energy changes happen in a car braking to a stop?
c: chemical potential energy → thermal → kinetic → electrical energy
kinetic energy → thermal energy (heating the brakes)
items.e: A car braking to a stop: kinetic energy → thermal energy (heating the brakes).

items.q: Which energy changes happen in a solar cell?
c: chemical potential energy → thermal → kinetic → electrical energy
gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy
chemical potential energy → gravitational potential energy (and thermal)
items.e: A solar cell: light (radiant) energy → electrical energy.

items.q: What is power?
c: the rate of work done or energy transferred

items.q: A car engine is 30% efficient. Where does most of the wasted energy go?
Is solar energy a renewable or a non-renewable energy resource?
c: neither: it is not an energy resource
items.e: A renewable resource is replaced naturally and will not run out; fossil fuels and nuclear fuel will run out.

items.q: A load gains 9000 J of gravitational potential energy when it is raised 15 m. What is its mass? (g = 10 N/kg)

The speed of a car doubles. What happens to its kinetic energy?
c: It becomes four times as large.
items.e: KE = ½mv², so doubling v multiplies KE by 2² = 4.

items.q: A kettle is supplied with 1000 J and gives 400 J of useful energy. What is its efficiency?
A motor is supplied with 1000 J and gives 900 J of useful energy. What is its efficiency?
A car engine is supplied with 200 J and gives 60 J of useful energy. What is its efficiency?
A motor is supplied with 500 J and transfers 250 J usefully. How much energy is wasted?
items.e: Energy is conserved: wasted = total − useful.

items.q: A kettle gives 600 J of useful energy with an efficiency of 30%. How much energy is supplied to it?
A motor gives 50 J of useful energy with an efficiency of 10%. How much energy is supplied to it?
A motor is supplied with 1000 J and transfers 250 J usefully. How much energy is wasted?
items.e: Energy is conserved: wasted = total − useful.

items.q: A motor takes in 2000 J and gives 800 J of useful energy. How much energy is wasted (mostly as heat)?
items.e: 2000 − 800 = 1200 J; it is not destroyed, just not useful.

items.q: Jia Hui's toy car uses 250 J of energy and gives 225 J of useful energy. What is its efficiency?
A solar panel is supplied with 2000 J and gives 400 J of useful energy. What is its efficiency?

A solar panel takes in 800 J and gives 320 J of useful energy. How much energy is wasted (mostly as heat)?
items.e: 800 − 320 = 480 J; it is not destroyed, just not useful.

items.q: A power station gives 900 J of useful energy with an efficiency of 90%. How much energy is supplied to it?
How much energy does an iron (1000 W) transfer in 300 s?
How much energy does a television (100 W) transfer in 10 s?
A pendulum swings. At which point is its kinetic energy greatest?
c: at the lowest point of the swing
items.e: GPE is smallest there, so KE is largest.

items.q: A 2 kg ball falls from rest through 1.8 m. Ignoring air resistance, what is its speed just before it hits the ground? (g = 10 N/kg)
A crane lifts a 500 kg load 20 m in 40 s. What is its useful power? (g = 10 N/kg)
A ball dropped from 2 m bounces back to only 1.5 m. Why?
c: Some energy is transferred to thermal energy and sound in the bounce.
items.e: Energy is conserved but some is wasted.

items.q: A 0.5 kg stone is thrown straight up at 4 m/s. Ignoring air resistance, how high does it rise? (g = 10 N/kg)
items.e: ½mv² = mgh, so h = v² ÷ 2g = 16 ÷ 20 = 0.8 m.

items.q: A 50 kg skateboarder rolls down a 2 m ramp from rest. Ignoring friction, what is her kinetic energy at the bottom? (g = 10 N/kg)
Which energy changes happen in a hydroelectric power station?
c: chemical potential energy → electrical → light and thermal energy
gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy
items.e: A hydroelectric power station: gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy.

items.q: A 60 kg student runs up stairs 3 m high in 5 s. What is her useful power output? (g = 10 N/kg)
A 2 kg stone is thrown straight up at 10 m/s. Ignoring air resistance, how high does it rise? (g = 10 N/kg)
items.e: ½mv² = mgh, so h = v² ÷ 2g = 100 ÷ 20 = 5 m.

items.q: Which fuel generates about 95% of Singapore's electricity?
items.e: Natural gas is the cleanest fossil fuel, but it is still non-renewable.

Two students of equal mass run up the same stairs. A takes 5 s and B takes 10 s. Which is true?
c: Both do the same work, but A has twice the power.
A does twice as much work.
